steps.say: The app writes each event to an outbox row.
The sender reads a row and posts it.
If the post fails, the row waits and tries again.

rows.why: One row holds all state for one event.
It spares a service that is down.
A person can inspect parked rows later.

chapters.title: How a worker claims and parks a row
chapters.prose:
Each worker takes one row with a lock and skips rows that are already locked. This stops two workers from sending the same event.

A failed post adds one to the try count in the same row. After 5 tries the worker marks the row as parked and stops.

Risk

A crash after the post but before the commit sends the event twice. The receiver must ignore an event id it has seen.

decisions.decision: How a worker claims a row
decisions.why: The lock cannot go stale after a crash.

chapters.title: How retries are spaced
chapters.prose:
The delay doubles after each failed try, up to a cap of 10 minutes. A service that is down gets less load as the outage grows.
